name: Creavit Studio
subcategory: AI image and video generation suite
tagline: A browser based AI creative studio for generating and editing images and video from prompts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The interface layer here is not the hard part: prompt box, model picker, aspect ratio presets, a gallery, some editing tools. An agent can put that in front of a hosted inference API in an afternoon and you will have something you actually use. The catch is that you are not replacing the product, you are replacing its front end while renting the same class of GPUs underneath, and you pay per generation instead of per month. If the studio's real appeal is a curated set of tuned models, style presets and one-click workflows that someone else tested for you, your build will feel noticeably rawer for the first week. Worth it if you generate in bursts, a bad trade if you generate all day and hate credit math.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that sends prompts and reference images to a hosted image and video model API, tracks jobs, and files every result in a searchable local gallery with the parameters that produced it.
requirements: An inference provider API key (Replicate or fal.ai) with a funded balance
Node 20 and a local machine you don't mind leaving on for long video jobs
Disk space, generated media gets fat quickly
whatYouLose: Curated model lineup and presets someone else already tuned and tested
Fast iterative editing tools: inpainting brushes, masking, layer style UI
Flat monthly cost predictability, you are on per-second GPU billing now
Hosted storage, sharing links and anything resembling a team workflow
Whatever the service does to keep up as new models ship every few weeks
moatNotes: The defensible bits are the editing UX and the fact that someone else eats GPU capacity risk. Model weights are mostly rented by everyone, including you.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a prompt box is easy and everything around it is not. Masking, inpainting, upscaling, consistent characters, retrying a failed video job without paying twice: that is a lot of small UI work, and a paid studio has already done it and keeps redoing it as models change. People also pay to stop thinking about credits, quotas and provider outages. A DIY build wins when your usage is narrow and repetitive, and loses when you want to sit down and explore for three hours.
notes: You can clone the wrapper in a weekend, you cannot clone the GPU bill.
prompt:
Build a local AI media studio as a single Next.js 15 app (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind). No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry. Runs on my machine only.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 + TypeScript + Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for job and asset metadata
- Generated files written to ./media on disk, served through a route handler
- Replicate as the only inference provider, token in .env as REPLICATE_API_TOKEN

Features in scope:
1. Generate page: prompt textarea, optional negative prompt, model dropdown (three image models, one video model, hardcoded in a models.ts config with their input schemas), aspect ratio presets, seed field, batch count 1 to 4.
2. Submit creates a job row (queued), calls Replicate, polls until done, downloads the output to ./media, stores width/height/model/params/cost estimate.
3. Library page: grid of all assets, filter by model and date, full text search over prompts, click for a detail drawer showing every parameter with a "remix this" button that refills the generate form.
4. Image to image and upscale: upload or pick an existing asset as input, run it through an img2img or upscale model.
5. Presets: named saved parameter bundles stored in SQLite, applied to the form in one click. Ship four starter presets.
6. A jobs panel showing running, failed and finished jobs with the raw provider error text on failure, and a retry button.
7. A spend page: sum of estimated cost per model per month, from the stored estimates.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, sharing links, inpainting brush or mask editor, team features, mobile app, payment handling, any analytics.

Deliverables: working app, .env.example, README with setup in under ten lines, and seeded models.ts. Handle long running video jobs without blocking the UI: poll from the client against a status route. If a download fails, keep the job row and mark it errored rather than crashing.
